questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Give reasons for the rise to power of President Paul Biya in 1982.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Paul Biya became President of Cameroon on 6 November 1982, two days after Ahidjo announced his resignation. Any seven reasons are accepted.

1. *Constitutional succession.* A constitutional amendment of 1975 made the Prime Minister the successor of the President if the post became vacant; Biya had been Prime Minister since 1975.
2. *Ahidjo's resignation (4 November 1982),* officially for health reasons, left the post open to him.
3. *Ahidjo's trust.* Ahidjo chose and supported him as a loyal and discreet collaborator, and expected to keep influence as head of the party.
4. *Administrative experience.* He had served as Director of the civil cabinet and Secretary-General of the Presidency (from 1968) and as a Minister, so he knew the state machinery.
5. *Regional balance.* A southerner (Beti) succeeding a northerner (Fulani) satisfied the principle of balance between the regions.
6. *Support of the single party (the CNU)* and of the National Assembly, which accepted the transfer without opposition.
7. *Support of the army and administration* and of France, which preferred a smooth constitutional transfer.
8. *Reputation as an intellectual and technocrat,* seen as calm and acceptable to most groups.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Why did the military attempt to overthrow Paul Biya in 1984 fail?

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The coup attempt of 6 April 1984 was led by officers of the Republican Guard, many from the north and thought to be loyal to former President Ahidjo. It failed for these reasons (any seven):

1. *Loyalty of the regular army.* Most of the army, gendarmerie and police stayed loyal to the President and to the Chief of Staff and fought the rebels.
2. *Poor planning and coordination.* The plotters did not capture the President or key points quickly, and units did not act together.
3. *Lack of popular support.* The population did not rise to support them, and they did not control the radio for long enough to persuade the nation.
4. *Quick response of Biya.* He appeared in public, broadcast a message and reorganised the loyal forces.
5. *Assistance of foreign friends,* especially France, which backed the legal government.
6. *Division among the rebels* and uncertainty about who would lead after the coup.
7. *Underestimation of the loyalty of the other units,* including the gendarmerie and units outside the capital.
8. *Heavy fighting* in Yaoundé ended in the defeat of the rebels, many of whom were arrested and sentenced.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) State the achievements of President Paul Biya in Cameroon between 1982 and 2019.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any six achievements are accepted.

1. *Political liberalisation.* The return to multiparty politics (laws of December 1990), the creation of many parties and a free press; the CNU became the Cameroon People's Democratic Movement (CPDM) in 1985.
2. *Constitutional reforms.* The 1996 constitution created regions and the Senate (set up in 2013); the National Dialogue of 2019 led to a special status for the North-West and South-West.
3. *Economic reforms.* Structural adjustment from the late 1980s, and debt relief when Cameroon reached the completion point of the HIPC initiative (2006).
4. *Infrastructure.* New roads and bridges (for example the Douala-Yaoundé highway and the second Wouri bridge), dams (Lom Pangar, Memve'ele) and the deep-sea port of Kribi.
5. *Education and health.* The creation of new state universities in the early 1990s (Buea, Douala, Dschang, Ngaoundéré, Yaoundé II) and the expansion of schools and health centres.
6. *Settlement of the Bakassi dispute* with Nigeria after the 2002 ruling of the International Court of Justice and the Greentree Agreement (2006), with the transfer of Bakassi in 2008.
7. *Regional security.* Cameroon took part in the regional force against Boko Haram from 2015.
8. *Development strategies,* such as Vision 2035 (Cameroon Emergence).
